title: Manipulation of Topological Corner States via Subchiral Symmetry
authors: Hai-Tao Ding, Tianqi Chen, Leong-Chuan Kwek, Jiangbin Gong
abstract: Higher-order topological phases provide robust corner modes, but their use requires controllable creation, isolation, and transfer of individual modes and their superpositions. Here we demonstrate, using the two-dimensional Benalcazar-Bernevig-Hughes model as an example, that subchiral symmetry provides a general control principle for manipulating topological corner modes. The conventional chiral symmetry decomposes into four subchiral symmetries, each associated with one zero-energy corner mode. By selectively breaking these subsymmetries with controlled intercell hoppings, we reduce the fourfold corner-state manifold step by step to single isolated modes. We further design adiabatic protocols that transfer either a single corner state or a superposition of two corner states between selected corners, while preserving the relative phase in the latter case. Both numerical simulations and IBM quantum-processor implementations show that the proposed protocols can be executed with high fidelity, establishing subchiral symmetry as a route to programmable higher-order topological state manipulation.
summary: The paper introduces subchiral symmetry as a general control principle for manipulating the corner modes found in higher-order topological insulators using the 2D BBH model. By selectively breaking these symmetries, researchers can isolate individual zero-energy states and execute adiabatic protocols to coherently transfer both single modes and superpositions of two modes. This capability was successfully demonstrated on an IBM quantum processor, establishing a pathway for programmable topological state control.
main_problem: The core problem is developing a general, controllable principle for manipulating topological corner modes (zero-energy states) in higher-order topological insulators (SOTIs). This requires selectively creating, isolating, and coherently transferring these degenerate modes.
main_result: Subchiral symmetry was established as the control mechanism, allowing for the stepwise reduction of fourfold zero-mode manifolds to single isolated modes. Furthermore, adiabatic protocols successfully transferred both single modes and coherent superpositions of two modes with high fidelity on quantum hardware.
method: The work combines theoretical analysis using symmetry protection (subchiral symmetry) with experimental validation via time-dependent Hamiltonian engineering and implementation on an IBM quantum processor.
model_or_system: The primary model is the two-dimensional Benalcazar–Bernevig–Hughes (BBH) model, a paradigmatic SOTI. The control is achieved by selectively breaking the four associated subchiral symmetries using controlled intercell hoppings in the Hamiltonian.
key_observables: Zero-energy corner states, single/superposition state transfer fidelity ($F^*$), and density distributions $P(x, y)$ showing mode localization.
important_parameters: The control strength of the subchiral symmetry breaking terms ($H_\alpha$) and the adiabatic evolution time scale ($T$).
main_assumptions: The ability to realize and maintain phase coherence during state transfer protocols on physical quantum hardware (IBM processor).
figures_summary: Figures detail the energy spectrum showing stepwise lifting of zero modes using symmetry breaking, and density plots/fidelity curves demonstrating successful single-mode and superposition state transfer between corners.
paper_structure: The paper proceeds by first introducing the BBH model and its fourfold degenerate corner states. It then details how subchiral symmetries provide a control principle for sequentially isolating these modes. Finally, it presents adiabatic protocols to coherently transfer both single and two-state superpositions of these modes, validated numerically and on quantum hardware.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses programmable topological dynamics by linking symmetry protection (subchiral symmetry) to physical state manipulation, which is highly relevant for designing robust quantum simulators or quantum memory elements based on topological materials.
